claims.text: Reliable formation of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials is governed by the synergistic effects of elemental distribution, lattice strain, and surface defects.
The catalytic performance of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials is governed by the synergistic effects of elemental distribution, lattice strain, and surface defects.
The effects of elemental distribution, lattice strain, and surface defects can be predicted and validated by combining in situ TEM experiments with molecular dynamics simulations.
Elemental distribution, lattice strain, and surface defects can be varied controllably through experimental synthesis and simulation methods.
An optimal elemental distribution improves catalytic activity relative to a random elemental distribution.
Optimal lattice strain improves catalytic activity relative to minimal lattice strain.
Optimal surface-defect populations improve catalytic activity relative to minimal surface defects.
Optimal elemental distribution, lattice strain, and surface defects enhance catalytic selectivity.
Optimal elemental distribution, lattice strain, and surface defects enhance catalytic stability.
